mathgap.title: Signed 'has N more than'
mathgap.principle: Interpret statements of the form 'X has N more than Y' as a signed difference: X = Y + N. This preserves the direction of the difference and correctly updates the counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly says 'X has N more than Y' (or 'X has N fewer than Y').
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has 5 more than Y' as X = Y - 5 (subtracting instead of adding).

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: When a transfer 'X gives N to Y' occurs, subtract N from X's count and add N to Y's count. This models the net effect of the transfer on each person's total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'X gives N to Y' (or equivalently 'Y receives N from X').
mathgap.example: Adding N to both X and Y when X gives N to Y, instead of subtracting from X and adding to Y.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a variable for each person and translate every relevant statement into a linear equation. Solve the resulting system simultaneously to obtain all unknown counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When multiple constraints involve the same set of variables and a unique solution is required.
mathgap.example: Solving each equation in isolation without considering how they interrelate, leading to inconsistent values.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by k times', treat it as multiplication: new X = k * original X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a phrase explicitly mentions a multiplicative increase (e.g., 'increases by 3 times').
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X increases by 3 times' as X = X + 3 instead of X = 3 * X.

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: If a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the splitter's final count to zero and give each recipient an equal share of the splitter's initial total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says a person distributes all of their items equally among several others.
mathgap.example: Assuming the splitter keeps some items after an equal split, rather than giving away the entire amount.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'difference between X and Y' as the signed difference X - Y, preserving the order given, rather than an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses the phrase 'difference between X and Y' without qualifiers such as 'absolute'.
mathgap.example: Treating 'difference between X and Y' as |X - Y|, losing the sign of the difference.

mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' in relational equations
mathgap.principle: In relational statements without a numeric amount, such as 'the number of X that Y has more than Z is equal to ...', treat the left side as a signed difference Y - Z.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational equation contains a phrase like 'Y has more than Z' but no explicit number.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Y has more than Z' as |Y - Z|, ignoring the direction of the difference.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Apply all transfer statements first, updating each person's count, then use the resulting final counts in relational equations. This ensures relational constraints refer to the correct (post‑transfer) amounts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When both transfer statements and relational equations appear in the same problem.
mathgap.example: Using relational equations with pre‑transfer counts, ignoring the effect of the transfers.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: Treat direct count statements (e.g., 'X has N items') as the initial amounts before any transfers occur. Subsequent transfers modify these initial values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a problem provides explicit counts for some individuals alongside transfer statements.
mathgap.example: Treating a given count as the final amount after transfers, thereby ignoring subsequent give‑away actions.

mathgap.title: Answer formatting
mathgap.principle: Output the final answer using the exact required format: 'The final answer is $\boxed{<integer>}$'. No extra text or formatting should be added.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When producing the final answer for any mathgap problem.
mathgap.example: Writing 'The answer is 42' instead of the required boxed LaTeX format.

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the given count already incorporates any later give‑away actions, ignoring that transfers modify the amounts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret direct counts as initial amounts before any transfers, then apply each transfer separately to update the counts.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may think the splitter retains some items after splitting or miscalculate the equal share.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a person splits all items equally among recipients, set the splitter's final count to zero and give each recipient the total divided by the number of recipients.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model adds the transferred amount to the giver and subtracts from the receiver, reversing the intended flow.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: For a statement 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has more than' in relational equations as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the sign and interprets the phrase as |X - Y|, losing the direction of the inequality.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'X has more than Y' as a signed difference X - Y, preserving the order of the names.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'difference between X and Y' as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the phrase denotes a magnitude only, ignoring the order of X and Y.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'difference between X and Y' as the signed expression X - Y, keeping the given order.
